To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gravitino production during reheating in split SUSY can be dominant over thermal contributions, and that the gravitino mass is constrained to be below 10^6 GeV for reheat temperatures below 10^8 GeV.

(i) in the context of Split supersymmetry the gravitino production during inflation is dominated by the production of gravitino-antisymmetric pairs from the interaction of the inflaton with the gravitino, (ii) this production can dominate over the thermal production of the gravitino from the decay of the sparticles, (iii) in this case, the gravitino abundance is independent on the supersymmetry scale, and is only determined by the reheating temperature,

the gravitinos produced from reheating in the split SUSY scenarios are typically non-thermal, that the supersymmetry-breaking scale of the relevant sectors is bounded from above by the reheat temperature and that a successful baryon asymmetry and a viable neutralinos can be produced if the gravitinos are non-thermal and the supersymmetry is broken at a scale below the reheat temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the production of gravitinos from the reheating process in split supersymetry, which is a natural scenario where the splitting between the particle masses and sparticle masses is much larger than TeV.
the production of gravitinos in the context of reheating in models of split supersymetry, and the implications of the production for baryogenesis and dark matter.
the production of gravitinos from thermal and nonthermal processes in the context of models with a large splitting between particle and supersymmetric partners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in split supersymmetries the gravitino production during reheating is the main contribution to the cosmological abundance of gravitinos.
in the context of the split supersymmetry the gravitino is the most natural candidate for dark matter, and that the supersymmetry is broken at a scale of order 100 TeV.
the gravitino production during reheating is an important and interesting process, which deserves more attention and study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the context of models where the splitting can be larger than a TeV, the production of gravitinos from reheating can dominate over thermal contributions and can be important for baryogenesis and dark matter.

in split supersymmetries with a large mass splitting between particle and superparticle masses, the thermal gravitino abundance is not a serious problem for the reheating temperature as high as the supersymmetry scale.
gravitino production during reheating is an important process in the context of models where supersymmetry is broken above the TeV scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gravitino abundance can be significantly increased by the nonthermal contribution from reheating and the thermal production of gravitinos can be negligible.
the production of gravitinos from reheating in a supersymmetric model can be very efficient and may lead to interesting cosmological consequences.
gravitino production in the split supersymmetry scenario can be very efficient, even if the supersymmetry scale is as large as a few tens of TeVs.
